column1: # Static --cutoff sweep vs the current dynmul-driven default. With dynmul>0
# (compiled default dynmul=7) the static --cutoff is IGNORED (yals.c) --
# budget is purely dynamic, each probe starting at 1000 flips and every
# probe-best improvement extending the deadline to D*(flips-so-far). This
# sweep asks whether a flat static cutoff can match/beat that dynamic
# default, and if so where the best flat value sits. `default` is the
# baseline (dynmul=7, cutoff irrelevant); the dyn0_* rows force dynmul=0
# (flat --cutoff every probe, no dynamic extension) across a log-ish range
